 Shri Manish Yadav, - Advocate for the appellant.

High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri Ajay Raj Gupta - Pl for the respondent/State.
_ __ Learned counsel for the appellant seeks to withdraw I.A. no. 8374/2023.
Accordingly, the same stands dismissed as withdrawn.
Heard on I.A. no. 6891/2023 which is an application filed under section 389 (1) of Cr.P.C on behalf of appellant Anil for grant of bail and suspension of remaining jail sentence.
2/ The appellant has been convicted under section 376(2)(i) of IPC and sentenced to undergo 10 years R.I with fine of Rs. 100/- with default stipulation.
3/ Learned counsel for the appellant contended that the appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this offence.
He has already completed 50% jail sentence of the awarded sentence.
As per the jail certificate, his conduct has been found good inside the jail.
There is strong case in favour of the appellant.
Final disposal of the appeal will take considerable long time.
Under these circumstances, he prays that the application be allowed and the remaining jail sentence of the appellant be suspended till final disposal of the appeal.

4/ Learned GA for the respondent/State opposed the prayer for grant of bail and suspension of remaining jail sentence of the appellant by submitting that the appellant has been properly convicted and sentenced by the trial Court.

5/ Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, arguments advanced by both the parties as also taking note of the fact that the appellant has already suffered jail incarceration for the period of 5  years and with remission, he has completed more than six years and three months jail sentence out of the awarded sentence; he has been acquitted from the charge under the POCSO Act and final disposal of appeal is likely to take time, I deem it proper to suspend the remaining jail Anil Kumar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193758653/

sentences.text: Accordingly, IA No. 6891/2023 is allowed and the execution of remaining jail sentence of the appellant is hereby suspended till the final disposal of this appeal and it is ordered that the appellant be released on bail upon his depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, and upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.75,000/- with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, with a further direction to appear before the Registry of this Court on 11/12//2023 and on such other dates, as may be fixed by the Registry of this Court in this regard during the pendency of this appeal.
List the matter in due course.
